catalog_quote: [p.19 n.30] Huechý, yo fui, he sido, &c. Mechý, tu fuiste, &c. Nechý, aquel fue, &c. ... En dicho tiempo se haze siẽpre el acento en la, y, vltima, por diferenciarlo de el presente de sujuntiuo, que es lo mismo. [p.20 n.32] Tambien vsan este tiempo sin expressar la m, haziendo el acento en la e; v.g. Serè bueno, pocme huèchi. Seràs bueno, pocme mèchi. Serà bueno, pocmeèchy, y assi los demas. [p.24 n.49] GERVNDIOS de Genitiuo. Echtopor, de ser, estàr, &c. Auechtopòr, de ser tu, estàr, &c. Yuechtopòr, de estàr aquel. ... Es necessario, que se haga el acento en la vltima vocal, para distinguirlo del gerundio de datiuo; v.g. Estoy cansado de estàr en mi labrança, huamapiaù echtopò, techequetaze huaze. [p.25 n.50] GERVNDIO DE datiuo. Este se forma con la particula, topo, acentuada en la primera vocal; v.g. Vechtòpo, para ser yo. Auechtòpo, para ser tu. Yuechtòpo, para ser aquel.

new_statements.translation: [n.30] In this tense [the perfect Huechý 'I was', Mechý, Nechý ...] the accent is always placed on the final y, to differentiate it from the present subjunctive, which is otherwise identical. [n.49] Genitive gerunds: Echtopòr 'of being' ... It is necessary that the accent be placed on the last vowel, to distinguish it from the dative gerund. [n.50] Dative gerund: this is formed with the particle topo, accented on the first vowel; e.g. Vechtòpo 'for me to be', Auechtòpo 'for you to be'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: No general statement of where word accent falls exists in any accessible description. The 1683 grammar treats accent as distinctive and morphologically conditioned: certain inflections require final accent (perfect -ý; genitive gerund -topò(r); future -chì 'haziendo el acento en la e', p.20 n.32) while a homographic suffix takes accent on its first vowel (dative gerund -tòpo). Accent is otherwise only marked graphically (grave accents on example words, on final, penultimate and other syllables) without explanation. The modern sketch (Álvarez 2018, seen only second-hand) reportedly states that the missionary texts do not allow the stressed syllable to be identified.
new_statements.exceptions: Only the morphological minimal pairs above (perfect vs. present subjunctive; genitive vs. dative gerund). No lexical exceptions or default position given.
new_statements.domain_note: Statements concern individual inflected verb forms (citation forms in paradigms); nothing on phrase-level prominence. Language extinct since the 19th c; no instrumental or modern first-hand data possible.
new_statements.identity_note: Yangues 1683 (edited and published by Ruiz Blanco) describes the 'lengua cummanagota' of the Franciscan Píritu missions (Cumanagotos, Píritus, Palenques; Ruiz Blanco's appended dictionary flags Palenque-specific words). Tauste 1680, also checked, is primarily a Chaima grammar (a separate Glottolog languoid) that the author says is also understood by Cumanagotos etc. Modern revitalisation literature calls the macro-variety 'choto maimu(ru)' / 'caribe septentrional' / 'Itoto Majun'.

new_statements.translation: [p.19 n.30] In this tense the accent is always placed on the final y, to distinguish it from the present subjunctive, which is the same [form]. [p.20 n.32] They also use this tense without expressing the m, placing the accent on the e; e.g. 'I shall be good', pocme huechí. [p.24 n.49] It is necessary that the accent be placed on the final vowel, to distinguish it from the dative gerund. [p.25 n.50] This [dative gerund] is formed with the particle topo, accented on the first vowel; e.g. Vechtopo, 'for me to be'.

VechtopOy, para fer yo'. Differences are scanned only (long s, hyphenation, 'hütchi' for 'huechí', 'topOy' for 'topo,'). A whole-fil…
new_statements.relation_note: Agrees with the existing statement (same four Yangues passages, same 'unclear' reading) and with the catalog's empty rule. Adds the negative result that the other two works in the Platzmann set, Ruiz Blanco's Arte y tesoro (vol. 3) and Tauste's Arte (vol. 1), say nothing about accent or stress: the only 'acento' hits in the 862 kB scanned of the whole three-volume set are the four Yangues passages.
new_statements.rule_in_words: No general rule for word accent is stated in any of the three volumes. Only Yangues (vol. 2) mentions accent, and only as a diacritic device for four specific verb forms: final-syllable accent on the preterite in -y (huechý 'I was') and on the genitive gerund in -topór (echtopòr), accent on the -e of the m-less future (huechí/pocme huechí), and first-vowel accent on the dative gerund tópo (véchtopo). Ruiz Blanco's Arte (vol. 3) describes the same preterite (-y, n. 33) and gerunds (topo, nn. 43-45, 66) with no mention of accent, and neither it nor Tauste's Arte (vol. 1) has a letters/pronunciation chapter that addresses stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Accent remarks are morpheme-specific (preterite -y, future -e, gerunds -topór vs tópo) and serve to disambiguate homographic forms; no default placement and no exceptions to one are given. Grave accents are printed on many Cumanagoto forms in the 1683 original, but the Google scanned of this reprint drops them.
new_statements.identity_note: Yangues 1683 and Ruiz Blanco 1690 describe the Cumanagoto-Palenque variety of the Píritu missions (Ruiz Blanco marks Palenque terms 'P' in his Diccionario and notes six or more synonymous ways of speaking across territories). Tauste 1680 (Platzmann vol. 1) is primarily a grammar of Chaima of the Cumaná province, presented as one language with the Cumanagotos, Cores, Parias etc., differing in pronunciation by adding or dropping syllables. Álvarez 2018 (not opened) treats Cumanagoto, Chaima, Palenque, Guaiquerí and Pariagoto as one language, 'choto maimuru'.
